beats.text: When you arrive, Earth's calendar has moved on by about 26,000 years. Remember that number. It's about to look small.

beats.text: Real ships can't just jump to a speed. So for the last trip, picture an engine that pushes at exactly 1 g, Earth's gravity, the whole way. On board, you'd feel at home.

beats.text: And the Andromeda Galaxy, 2.5 million light-years away, takes just 28.6 years on your clock.

beats.text: At the halfway point, you'd be moving at 99.99999999997% of the speed of light. 12 nines. Faster than any proton in the Large Hadron Collider.

beats.text: Could anyone build that engine? Not with anything we know how to make. The energy alone is about 82 million years of humanity's total supply. But relativity itself doesn't say no.

alt_titles: What You'd See at 99.9999% the Speed of Light
What If You Flew at 99.9999% Light Speed?
metadata.hook: What would you actually see, feel and survive if you traveled at 99.9999% of the speed of light? We turn the dial one nine at a time, from 10% to 99.9999%, with a real star catalog bent by relativity on screen.
learn: Why the whole sky collapses into one patch ahead of you, and why the famous starbow ring is a myth
How fast your clock runs compared to Earth's at every speed
Which speed turns empty space into a lethal radiation beam
What each extra nine costs in energy
How far you could really get in one lifetime, and what you'd come home to
metadata.summary: Every level shows your clock against Earth's, what you see out the window, what hits the front of the ship, and the energy bill, all computed in code from the sources below.
key_numbers: At 99.9999% of light speed: 1 year on board = 707 years on Earth
At 90%: each hydrogen atom carries 1.21 GeV; unshielded, a lethal dose in under half a second
At 99.99%: half the sky fits in a circle 1.6° wide, and the cosmic microwave background ahead reaches 385 K
Energy for an ISS-mass ship at 99.9999%: about 45,000 years of world energy use
1 g ship to Andromeda: 28.6 years on board; round trip 57 years for you, 5 million years on Earth
metadata.assumptions: Assumptions: an ISS-mass ship cruising at a fixed speed (energy is the minimum, perfect engine, no fuel); typical interstellar gas of about 1 hydrogen atom per cm³; dose figures are unshielded lower bounds; the Andromeda trip uses constant 1 g acceleration with a midpoint flip.
